changelogEntry: 1.3.0 - Paradee-8M v1.1 replaces v1.0 as the TTS: paradee-8m-v1_1.gguf, converted with elizaOS/llama.cpp tools/paradee/convert_paradee_pt_to_gguf.py --version 1.1 (byte-reproducible). v1.1 keeps v1.0's text side and replaces the iSTFTNet generator with a frame-rate source-filter head (seeded noise, deterministic output); libelizainference routes on the GGUF's paradee.decoder.head key, so a v1.0 file still loads. On a Lenovo TB336FU it runs about 3x faster than v1.0 with about 70 MB peak private memory instead of 202 MB and the same WER (elizaOS/llama.cpp#86). The row id changes, so a device that staged tts/paradee/ with v1.0 re-stages it. The misaki, eSpeak NG, Phonon-2 and VAD rows are unchanged from 1.2.0.

changelogEntry: 1.2.0 - Qwen3-ASR-0.6B is removed as a speech-recognition option: the text GGUF and mmproj rows are gone and ELIZA_ASR_BACKEND=qwen3 no longer stages them. Phonon-2 (Parakeet-TDT 0.6B, five-value) is the only local ASR: asr/phonon-2-fv5.gguf on libelizainference's parakeet backend (batch + streaming). A device that staged asr/ with the Qwen3-ASR pair re-stages it with Phonon-2. Phonon-2 weights are CC-BY-4.0: ship the attribution and NOTICE. The GGUF is unpublished; build it with packages/app/scripts/voice/build-phonon2-gguf.ts, which converts the pinned FermionResearch/Phonon-2 revision and checks every sha256. Paradee-8M stays the TTS; the Paradee, misaki and eSpeak NG rows are unchanged from 1.1.0.

changelogEntry: 1.1.0 - Phonon-2 (Parakeet-TDT 0.6B, five-value) is the default mobile ASR: asr/phonon-2-fv5.gguf on libelizainference's parakeet backend (batch + streaming, elizaOS/llama.cpp tools/parakeet). The Qwen3-ASR-0.6B pair stays in the catalog and is staged instead only with ELIZA_ASR_BACKEND=qwen3. Phonon-2 weights are CC-BY-4.0: ship the attribution and NOTICE. The GGUF is unpublished and is staged by converting the pinned FermionResearch/Phonon-2 revision (sha256-checked). The Paradee GGUF is staged as tts/paradee/paradee-8m-v1_0.gguf (the name the fused library, ElizaBionicInferenceServer and paradee-voice use); the Paradee GGUF and misaki lexicon rows carry their byte-reproducible pins; the eSpeak NG 1.52.0 English data (7 files, GPL-3.0-or-later, flagged) is staged under tts/paradee/espeak-ng-data/ so misaki pronounces words outside its lexicon.
